teaching.hint: What does changing a bit cost in the objective, and which changes can repair the required count?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Starting at num1 gives zero disagreement; the popcount mismatch can be repaired with only additions or only removals at the least significant eligible positions.
solution_outline.approach: Count the required one-bits. If num1 has too few, set its lowest unset bits until the count matches; if it has too many, clear its lowest set bits. Leave it unchanged when counts already match.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every edit changes the one-count in the needed direction. Among eligible edits made so far, the chosen positions have the least available XOR costs.
solution_outline.correctness: If additions are needed, any solution with removals also needs extra additions; deleting such a removal/addition pair lowers cost while preserving net count. Thus an optimum uses exactly the deficit in additions. Exchanging a chosen high unset bit with a lower unset bit strictly reduces XOR, forcing the lowest eligible bits. The removal case is symmetric. The count constraint is met and no other selection costs less.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(W)` time and `O(1)` space for the bounded bit width W, at most 31 relevant positions here.
solution_outline.pitfall: Sacrifice the lowest eligible bits, not the highest: high-bit disagreement dominates low-bit savings.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained positivity, fixed one-bit count, uniqueness, ordinary XOR minimization, and input bounds.
common_wrong_turns: Sacrifice the lowest eligible bits, not the highest: high-bit disagreement dominates low-bit savings.
